attend:1.en: A notice board on the Crosswind Plaza read: ALL CREW MUST *ATTEND* THE CAPTAIN'S BRIEFING AT DAWN. Old Helm folded his arms. Silverfang had posted it. She had no right to call our crew anywhere. Yet her briefings, everyone admitted, had never once been a waste of time.
attend:1.cnHint: 银牙在广场张贴告示，要求所有船员____她黎明前的简报会。
attend:1.hook: Old Helm read it twice, then began walking toward the meeting point.
attend:1.line: 'All crew must *attend* — yes, even yours, Old Helm.'

sentences.en: A notice board on the Crosswind Plaza read: ALL CREW MUST *ATTEND* THE CAPTAIN'S BRIEFING AT DAWN.
Old Helm folded his arms.
sentences.cn: 老舵抱起了胳膊。

sentences.en: Silverfang had posted it.
sentences.cn: 是银牙贴的。

sentences.en: She had no right to call our crew anywhere.
sentences.cn: 她没权利把我们的船员往任何地方召集。

sentences.en: Yet her briefings, everyone admitted, had never once been a waste of time.
sentences.cn: 可大家都承认，她的简报从来不浪费时间。

belief:1.en: Silverfang leaned against the harbour post, arms crossed, watching our troupe unload supplies. 'Your *belief* that friendship beats a contract is sweet,' she said, tossing a coin in the air. 'But out past the Redwind Gap, sweet gets you nowhere.' She caught the coin and smiled — not unkindly.
belief:1.cnHint: 银牙在港口挑战老船长，质疑他对____的坚持是否经得起考验。
belief:1.hook: The coin she tossed landed showing a map — a real one.
belief:1.line: 'Your *belief* in friendship is sweet, but the Redwind Gap is not.'

sentences.en: Silverfang leaned against the harbour post, arms crossed, watching our troupe unload supplies.
sentences.cn: 银牙靠在港口的柱子上，双臂交叉，看着我们的剧团卸货。

sentences.en: 'Your *belief* that friendship beats a contract is sweet,' she said, tossing a coin in the air.
'But out past the Redwind Gap, sweet gets you nowhere.'
sentences.cn: "但在红风隙外面，温情一文不值。"

sentences.en: She caught the coin and smiled — not unkindly.
sentences.cn: 她接住了硬币，笑了——不是不友善的那种。

carry:1.en: The morning trade bell rang across Ashpetal Wharf. Each member of our troupe had to *carry* a crate of wind-stones to the exchange booth before the bell rang again. Bell ran. I ran. Old Helm walked — and somehow arrived first, stones unspilt, humming a quiet tune.
carry:1.cnHint: 清晨，我们的队伍要在钟声结束前____风石箱到交易亭，老船长的方式出乎意料。
carry:1.hook: Old Helm set his crate down and said only, 'Pace wins.'
carry:1.line: '*Carry* it steady — hurry breaks more than it saves.'

sentences.en: The morning trade bell rang across Ashpetal Wharf.
sentences.cn: 晨间交易钟声在灰花码头响起。

sentences.en: Each member of our troupe had to *carry* a crate of wind-stones to the exchange booth before the bell rang again.
Bell ran.
sentences.cn: 小铃跑了。

sentences.en: I ran.
sentences.cn: 我跑了。

sentences.en: Old Helm walked — and somehow arrived first, stones unspilt, humming a quiet tune.
sentences.cn: 老舵走——却不知怎的率先到达，风石完好无损，哼着安静的小调。

else:1.en: After the others had chosen their sky-routes on the planning board, I stood there staring. Every path was marked: the safe ones, the fast ones, the scenic ones. Bell appeared beside me. 'Everyone *else* picks with their head,' she said softly, pressing a small compass into my palm. 'You pick with yours.'
else:1.cnHint: 规划路线时，其他人都做出了选择，领航员告诉我不必和____一样。
else:1.hook: The compass needle spun once and stopped, pointing somewhere new.
else:1.line: 'Everyone *else* has chosen — now it is your turn to decide.'

sentences.en: After the others had chosen their sky-routes on the planning board, I stood there staring.
sentences.cn: 其他人在规划板上选好了自己的飞行路线后，我站在那儿发呆。

sentences.en: Every path was marked: the safe ones, the fast ones, the scenic ones.
sentences.cn: 每条路都标好了：安全的、快速的、风景秀丽的。

sentences.en: Bell appeared beside me.
sentences.cn: 小铃在我身边出现了。

sentences.en: 'Everyone *else* picks with their head,' she said softly, pressing a small compass into my palm.
'You pick with yours.'
sentences.cn: "你用你的。"

prepare:1.en: The market square of Windhollow Island buzzed with colour. Silverfang's crew had arrived before us, and we could see them *preparing* their stall — laying out charts, polishing brass tools, stacking bright signal flags. Old Helm watched with calm eyes. 'They move fast,' Bell whispered. 'Then we move smarter,' he replied.
prepare:1.cnHint: 在风谷岛的集市广场，我们看到银牙的船员正在____他们的摊位，老舵手示意我们保持冷静。
prepare:1.hook: Whatever Silverfang was selling, every island captain wanted one.
prepare:1.line: 'We *prepare* our table before they open their mouths,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: The market square of Windhollow Island buzzed with colour.
sentences.cn: 风谷岛的市集广场色彩斑斓。

sentences.en: Silverfang's crew had arrived before us, and we could see them *preparing* their stall — laying out charts, polishing brass tools, stacking bright signal flags.
Old Helm watched with calm eyes.
sentences.cn: 老舵用平静的眼神观察着。

sentences.en: 'They move fast,' Bell whispered.
sentences.cn: "他们动作很快，"小铃低声说。

sentences.en: 'Then we move smarter,' he replied.
sentences.cn: "那我们就动得更聪明，"他回答。

workplace:1.en: Silverfang led us through the deck workshops of Ironhook Station, where crafters shaped map-glass under open sky. 'This is my *workplace*,' she said proudly, arms wide. Sparks drifted like tiny stars. Old Helm ran a finger along a finished chart and nodded slowly. Bell scribbled notes without looking up.
workplace:1.cnHint: 银牙带我们参观了铁钩站的甲板工坊，她自豪地称这里是她的____。
workplace:1.hook: One unfinished chart on the far bench carried a name none of us recognised.
workplace:1.line: 'Every corner of this *workplace* holds a secret,' Silverfang said softly.

sentences.en: Silverfang led us through the deck workshops of Ironhook Station, where crafters shaped map-glass under open sky.
sentences.cn: 银牙领我们穿过了铁钩站的甲板工坊，那里的工匠们在开阔的天空下打磨地图玻璃。

sentences.en: 'This is my *workplace*,' she said proudly, arms wide.
Sparks drifted like tiny stars.
sentences.cn: 火花像小星星一样飘落。

sentences.en: Old Helm ran a finger along a finished chart and nodded slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵用手指划过一张完成的海图，缓缓点了点头。

sentences.en: Bell scribbled notes without looking up.
sentences.cn: 小铃埋头记笔记，眼睛都没抬。

post:1.en: At the base of the great Wind-Needle pillar, travellers gathered to read notices. Silverfang had *posted* a bold challenge on the board: any troupe who could name three lost islands before sundown would win her finest chart. Old Helm read it twice. Bell grinned. I felt my pulse quicken.
post:1.cnHint: 银牙在风针柱的公告栏上____了一份大胆挑战书，老舵手仔细读了两遍。
post:1.hook: Sundown was less than two hours away.
post:1.line: 'I *post* this challenge for every troupe brave enough to answer,' Silverfang called out.

sentences.en: At the base of the great Wind-Needle pillar, travellers gathered to read notices.
sentences.cn: 在巨大的风针柱的底部，旅人们聚集在一起读告示。

sentences.en: Silverfang had *posted* a bold challenge on the board: any troupe who could name three lost islands before sundown would win her finest chart.
Old Helm read it twice.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍。

sentences.en: Bell grinned.
sentences.cn: 小铃咧嘴笑了。

sentences.en: I felt my pulse quicken.
sentences.cn: 我感觉心跳加快了。

complete:1.en: Silverfang spread the puzzle-chart across the stone table: a ring of islands with three pieces missing. 'Find the gaps,' she said. Old Helm studied it quietly, then placed one tile, then another, then a third. The map glowed faintly. '*Complete*,' he murmured. Silverfang's eyes went wide with surprise.
complete:1.cnHint: 银牙摆出一张残缺的拼图海图，老舵手一一填补空缺，将其____。
complete:1.hook: The glow faded — and revealed a path none of us had ever seen.
complete:1.line: 'At last the map is *complete*,' Old Helm said quietly.

sentences.en: Silverfang spread the puzzle-chart across the stone table: a ring of islands with three pieces missing.
sentences.cn: 银牙把谜题地图铺在石桌上：一圈岛屿，缺了三块。

sentences.en: 'Find the gaps,' she said.
sentences.cn: "找出缝隙，"她说。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied it quietly, then placed one tile, then another, then a third.
sentences.cn: 老舵静静地研究了一会儿，然后放下一块瓷砖，再放下一块，然后是第三块。

sentences.en: The map glowed faintly. '*Complete*,' he murmured.
Silverfang's eyes went wide with surprise.
sentences.cn: 银牙的眼睛睁得很大，吃惊不已。

measure:1.en: Bell stood at the edge of Drift Pier and stretched a long cord across the gap between two floating platforms. She *measured* the distance three times, muttering numbers. Silverfang leaned on a post nearby, watching with thin amusement. 'Trusting your rope more than your eyes?' she asked. Bell just smiled.
measure:1.cnHint: 贝尔在漂流码头边用绳子反复____两个浮台之间的距离，银牙在旁边冷眼旁观。
measure:1.hook: The gap was wider than any rope we carried.
measure:1.line: 'I always *measure* twice before I trust a bridge,' Bell said firmly.

sentences.en: Bell stood at the edge of Drift Pier and stretched a long cord across the gap between two floating platforms.
sentences.cn: 小铃站在漂流码头的边缘，在两个浮动平台之间拉紧了一根长绳。

sentences.en: She *measured* the distance three times, muttering numbers.
Silverfang leaned on a post nearby, watching with thin amusement.
sentences.cn: 银牙靠在附近的一根柱子上，用薄薄的笑意看着。

sentences.en: 'Trusting your rope more than your eyes?' she asked.
sentences.cn: "你相信绳子胜过眼睛？"她问。

sentences.en: Bell just smiled.
sentences.cn: 小铃只是笑了。

recommend:1.en: Outside the spice-stalls of Amber Arch, a friendly trader offered us three routes forward. Old Helm listened carefully, then turned to the trader. 'Which path do you *recommend* for a troupe carrying glass charts?' The trader paused, looked at our bags, and pointed without hesitation toward the high cloud road.
recommend:1.cnHint: 在琥珀拱廊的香料摊外，老舵手向一位商人询问哪条路线值得____。
recommend:1.hook: The cloud road had been closed for a season — until this morning.
recommend:1.line: 'I *recommend* the high road; the others have been restless lately,' the trader said.

sentences.en: Outside the spice-stalls of Amber Arch, a friendly trader offered us three routes forward.
sentences.cn: 琥珀拱廊的香料摊外，一个友善的商人给了我们三条前路。

sentences.en: Old Helm listened carefully, then turned to the trader.
sentences.cn: 老舵仔细听着，然后转向那商人。

sentences.en: 'Which path do you *recommend* for a troupe carrying glass charts?'
The trader paused, looked at our bags, and pointed without hesitation toward the high cloud road.
sentences.cn: 商人停顿了一下，看看我们的行囊，毫不犹豫地指向那条高云之路。

resource:1.en: Silverfang laid her cards on the table at Coppergate Crossing. 'Your troupe has heart,' she admitted, 'but heart is not a *resource* that fuels a ship.' Old Helm reached into his coat and set down three glowing word-shards. The light caught Silverfang's face. She was quiet for a long moment.
resource:1.cnHint: 在铜门路口，银牙说热情不是什么____，老舵手随即拿出三块发光的文字碎片回应她。
resource:1.hook: Silverfang had never seen word-shards glow that colour before.
resource:1.line: 'Courage is a fine *resource*, but charts keep you alive,' Silverfang said coolly.

sentences.en: Silverfang laid her cards on the table at Coppergate Crossing.
sentences.cn: 银牙在铜门渡口摊开了她的牌。

sentences.en: 'Your troupe has heart,' she admitted, 'but heart is not a *resource* that fuels a ship.'
Old Helm reached into his coat and set down three glowing word-shards.
sentences.cn: 老舵伸进外套，放下了三块闪闪发光的字晶。

sentences.en: The light caught Silverfang's face.
sentences.cn: 光线打在银牙的脸上。

sentences.en: She was quiet for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 她沉默了很久。

specific:1.en: Before the bet was sealed, Bell raised her hand. 'We need *specific* terms,' she said clearly, setting a small notebook on the barrel between us and Silverfang. 'Which islands count? Which charts are the prize?' Silverfang blinked, then laughed — a real laugh. 'Your navigator is sharper than you look,' she told Old Helm.
specific:1.cnHint: 在赌约正式定下之前，贝尔要求列出____的条款，让银牙刮目相看。
specific:1.hook: Silverfang picked up the pen and began to write something unexpected.
specific:1.line: 'Give me *specific* terms or the deal means nothing,' Bell said calmly.

sentences.en: Before the bet was sealed, Bell raised her hand.
sentences.cn: 赌注还没定下来，小铃就抬起了手。

sentences.en: 'We need *specific* terms,' she said clearly, setting a small notebook on the barrel between us and Silverfang.
'Which islands count?
sentences.cn: "哪些岛算数？

sentences.en: Which charts are the prize?'
sentences.cn: 哪些海图是赌注？"

sentences.en: Silverfang blinked, then laughed — a real laugh.
sentences.cn: 银牙眨了眨眼，然后笑了——真心实意的笑。

sentences.en: 'Your navigator is sharper than you look,' she told Old Helm.
sentences.cn: 她对老舵说，"你的航海员比你看起来聪明多了。"

positive:2.en: Bell spread a crinkled chart across the deck. Strange ink marks covered every corner. 'These aren't random,' she said quietly. Old Helm leaned in. The markings were *positive* signs — each one pointing toward the next island, like a trail of hopeful arrows left by someone who wanted us to follow.
positive:2.cnHint: 小铃在甲板上展开一张布满标记的旧图，发现这些符号都是____的指引。
positive:2.hook: But who had drawn them, and were they still watching?
positive:2.line: 'Every *positive* mark on this chart is a step someone took before us.'

sentences.en: Bell spread a crinkled chart across the deck.
sentences.cn: 小铃在甲板上铺开一张皱巴巴的海图。

sentences.en: Strange ink marks covered every corner.
sentences.cn: 奇怪的墨水符号覆盖了每个角落。

sentences.en: 'These aren't random,' she said quietly.
sentences.cn: 她轻声说，"这些不是随意画的。"

sentences.en: Old Helm leaned in.
sentences.cn: 老舵探了过去。

sentences.en: The markings were *positive* signs — each one pointing toward the next island, like a trail of hopeful arrows left by someone who wanted us to follow.

economic:2.en: We drifted into a small harbour island where merchants packed stalls along the edge of the cloud. Old Helm picked up a tiny ledger left on a crate. Its pages tracked the *economic* flow of the whole sky-route — which islands traded, which ones starved, which ones had simply vanished from the record.
economic:2.cnHint: 老舵主在市集中发现一本记录天空航线____往来的账本。
economic:2.hook: The last entry was dated the morning Silverfang first appeared.
economic:2.line: 'This *economic* record tells us more than any map ever could.'

sentences.en: We drifted into a small harbour island where merchants packed stalls along the edge of the cloud.
sentences.cn: 我们漂进了一个小港岛，商人们沿着云边摆满了摊位。

sentences.en: Old Helm picked up a tiny ledger left on a crate.
sentences.cn: 老舵捡起了一本遗留在木箱上的小账簿。

sentences.en: Its pages tracked the *economic* flow of the whole sky-route — which islands traded, which ones starved, which ones had simply vanished from the record.

link:2.en: Inside an old lighthouse on the edge of Amber Isle, Bell found a chain hanging from the ceiling. One ring was missing. She held it up and said the absent ring was the *link* between two halves of a hidden route — without it, the path split and led travelers in circles forever.
link:2.cnHint: 小铃在灯塔里发现一条断裂的链，那枚缺失的____牵连着一条隐秘的航路。
link:2.hook: Silverfang's ship had been circling this island for three days.
link:2.line: 'Find the missing *link* and the whole route opens up to us.'

sentences.en: Inside an old lighthouse on the edge of Amber Isle, Bell found a chain hanging from the ceiling.
sentences.cn: 在琥珀岛边缘的一座老灯塔里，小铃发现了一条从天花板吊下来的链子。

sentences.en: One ring was missing.
sentences.cn: 有一枚戒指不见了。

sentences.en: She held it up and said the absent ring was the *link* between two halves of a hidden route — without it, the path split and led travelers in circles forever.

produce:2.en: Old Helm handed me a small brass box found wedged beneath the helm. When I turned its key, the box began to *produce* a soft, rising hum that grew into a clear musical note. Bell pressed her ear close and whispered that the note matched the frequency the old star-charts used to mark safe passage.
produce:2.cnHint: 老舵主找到一只铜盒，转动钥匙后它____出一个与古老星图频率吻合的音符。
produce:2.hook: The hum grew louder the closer we steered toward the storm.
produce:2.line: 'It will *produce* the exact tone only when we are on the right path.'

sentences.en: Old Helm handed me a small brass box found wedged beneath the helm.
sentences.cn: 老舵递给我一个从舵下夹出来的小铜盒。

sentences.en: When I turned its key, the box began to *produce* a soft, rising hum that grew into a clear musical note.
Bell pressed her ear close and whispered that the note matched the frequency the old star-charts used to mark safe passage.
sentences.cn: 小铃把耳朵贴近了，低声说那音符的频率和古老星图用来标记安全航路的一样。

teach:2.en: Tucked inside a cracked wall on the Isle of Echoes, I found a short letter in a careful hand. A traveller had once paused here to *teach* a child the names of the star-roads, writing each one down so the lesson would last longer than memory. The final name on the list was one Old Helm had never heard.
teach:2.cnHint: 在回声岛的石缝里，我发现一封旅人留下的信，他曾在此____孩子认识星路的名字。
teach:2.hook: That last star-road name matched the symbol on Silverfang's flag.
teach:2.line: 'Someone chose to *teach* a child the very secret we are chasing.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside a cracked wall on the Isle of Echoes, I found a short letter in a careful hand.
sentences.cn: 在回声岛一道裂开的墙缝里，我找到了一封用工整笔迹写的短信。

sentences.en: A traveller had once paused here to *teach* a child the names of the star-roads, writing each one down so the lesson would last longer than memory.
The final name on the list was one Old Helm had never heard.
sentences.cn: 名单上的最后一个名字，是老舵从未听过的。

worth:2.en: Silverfang left a sealed pouch on our deck before dawn — no note, just a single glowing stone inside. Old Helm turned it over slowly. He said the stone was *worth* nothing as a gem, but as a key to the Tide Gate it was everything. His voice was steady, but his hands were not.
worth:2.cnHint: 竞争船长在甲板上留下一枚石头，老舵主说它作为宝石毫无价值，但作为潮汐门的钥匙____得上一切。
worth:2.hook: Accepting it meant accepting whatever deal came with it.
worth:2.line: 'It is *worth* more as a key than as anything else in the sky.'

sentences.en: Silverfang left a sealed pouch on our deck before dawn — no note, just a single glowing stone inside.
sentences.cn: 银牙在天亮前在我们的甲板上留下了一个密封的布袋——没有纸条，里面只有一块闪闪发光的石头。

sentences.en: Old Helm turned it over slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵缓缓转动着它。

sentences.en: He said the stone was *worth* nothing as a gem, but as a key to the Tide Gate it was everything.
His voice was steady, but his hands were not.
sentences.cn: 他的声音很平稳，但他的手在颤抖。

common:2.en: Bell lined up three maps from three different captains on the cabin table. At first glance they showed entirely different skies. But one feature appeared on every single one — a small blank circle drawn in the same corner. That blank was their only *common* mark, and it sat exactly where our compass refused to point.
common:2.cnHint: 小铃对比三位船长的航图，发现它们唯一____的标记是同一个空白圆圈。
common:2.hook: No captain had ever written a single word inside that circle.
common:2.line: 'The only *common* mark on all three maps is the one no one will explain.'

sentences.en: Bell lined up three maps from three different captains on the cabin table.
sentences.cn: 小铃在舱房的桌子上并排放了三张来自三位不同船长的地图。

sentences.en: At first glance they showed entirely different skies.
sentences.cn: 乍一看它们展示的天空完全不同。

sentences.en: But one feature appeared on every single one — a small blank circle drawn in the same corner.
sentences.cn: 但有一个特征出现在每一张上——同一个角落里画着一个小小的空白圆圈。

sentences.en: That blank was their only *common* mark, and it sat exactly where our compass refused to point.

daily:2.en: Wedged in a cleft on the morning-side of Cloud Shelf Isle, I found a small notebook. Someone had kept a *daily* record here — a few lines each dawn, tracking the wind, the light, and one repeating question written in the margin: 'Has it moved yet?' The final entry was yesterday.
daily:2.cnHint: 我在云礁岛发现一本笔记本，主人坚持____记录风向与光线，最后一页写于昨天。
daily:2.hook: Whatever 'it' was, the writer had never seen it move — until now.
daily:2.line: 'A *daily* record kept this long means someone is still waiting out there.'

sentences.en: Wedged in a cleft on the morning-side of Cloud Shelf Isle, I found a small notebook.
sentences.cn: 我在云架岛晨侧的一条岩隙里找到了一本小笔记本。

sentences.en: Someone had kept a *daily* record here — a few lines each dawn, tracking the wind, the light, and one repeating question written in the margin: 'Has it moved yet?'
The final entry was yesterday.
sentences.cn: 最后一条记录是昨天的。

policy:2.en: Inside the hollow of an ancient sky-tree, we found a rolled paper covered in tiny words. Old Helm spread it flat against the bark and read aloud. 'Every troupe must follow the island council's *policy*: one word earned, one gate opened. No exceptions.' The paper glowed faintly, then dissolved into our map.
policy:2.cnHint: 我们在天空古树的树洞里发现了一份岛屿议会的____，它规定了集字开门的规则。
policy:2.hook: But the gate ahead had already been opened by someone else.
policy:2.line: 'The island council's *policy* is clear — earn the word, or the gate stays shut.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow of an ancient sky-tree, we found a rolled paper covered in tiny words.
sentences.cn: 在一棵古老天空树的空心里，我们找到了一张卷起来的纸，上面密密麻麻地写满了字。

sentences.en: Old Helm spread it flat against the bark and read aloud.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它铺平贴着树皮读了出来。

sentences.en: 'Every troupe must follow the island council's *policy*: one word earned, one gate opened.
No exceptions.'
sentences.cn: 没有例外。"

sentences.en: The paper glowed faintly, then dissolved into our map.
sentences.cn: 纸张发出微弱的光，然后融进了我们的地图。

industry:2.en: The next island hummed with noise. Enormous fans spun in the wind, pipes carried coloured steam between towers, and workers in bright coats moved with steady purpose. Old Helm nodded approvingly. 'This whole island runs on *industry*,' he said. 'Every hand busy, every hour used.' Silverfang, watching from her ship's rail, looked less impressed.
industry:2.cnHint: 我们降落在一座充满机器轰鸣的岛屿，老舵长对这里繁忙的____赞叹不已。
industry:2.hook: Silverfang had visited this island before — and left in a hurry.
industry:2.line: 'I respect their *industry*, but something here does not feel right.'

sentences.en: The next island hummed with noise.
sentences.cn: 下一座岛屿嗡嗡作响。

sentences.en: Enormous fans spun in the wind, pipes carried coloured steam between towers, and workers in bright coats moved with steady purpose.
sentences.cn: 巨大的风车在风中旋转，管道在塔楼间传送彩色蒸汽，身穿亮色工装的工人步履坚定地忙碌着。

sentences.en: Old Helm nodded approvingly.
sentences.cn: 老舵赞许地点了点头。

sentences.en: 'This whole island runs on *industry*,' he said.
'Every hand busy, every hour used.'
sentences.cn: 每一双手都有事可做，每一刻都被充分利用。

sentences.en: Silverfang, watching from her ship's rail, looked less impressed.
sentences.cn: 银牙从自己的船栏杆上远眺，看起来兴致不高。

concern:2.en: Bell spread the new map fragment across the navigator's table and traced a thin dotted line toward a dark patch of cloud. Her brow creased. 'My only *concern*,' she said quietly, 'is that this route passes through the Storm Shelf. The clouds there do not move like normal clouds.' Outside, the wind had already changed direction.
concern:2.cnHint: 领航员小铃在研究新地图时，表达了对穿越暴风云区域的____。
concern:2.hook: The clouds on the map began to shift, slowly, on their own.
concern:2.line: 'My one *concern* is that storm — it does not behave like any I have charted.'

sentences.en: Bell spread the new map fragment across the navigator's table and traced a thin dotted line toward a dark patch of cloud.
sentences.cn: 小铃把新地图碎片铺在领航员的桌子上，用手指沿着一条细细的虚线描向一团乌云般的暗处。

sentences.en: Her brow creased.
sentences.cn: 她的眉头皱起来。

sentences.en: 'My only *concern*,' she said quietly, 'is that this route passes through the Storm Shelf.
The clouds there do not move like normal clouds.'
sentences.cn: 那里的云不像普通的云一样运动。

sentences.en: Outside, the wind had already changed direction.
sentences.cn: 外面的风已经改变了方向。

present:2.en: Silverfang came aboard without warning and set a small wooden box on our deck. 'A *present*,' she said, with a smile that showed too many teeth. Inside sat a compass that spun in all directions at once. Old Helm closed the box carefully and returned it. 'We find our own way,' he told her. She shrugged and sailed off.
present:2.cnHint: 银牙船长突然登船，给我们带来了一份奇怪的____，但老舵长婉言谢绝了。
present:2.hook: The compass inside the box was still spinning, even with the lid shut.
present:2.line: 'Consider it a *present* — though I do wonder if you are brave enough to use it.'

sentences.en: Silverfang came aboard without warning and set a small wooden box on our deck.
sentences.cn: 银牙没有预警就登上了我们的甲板，在甲板上放了一只小木盒。

sentences.en: 'A *present*,' she said, with a smile that showed too many teeth.
Inside sat a compass that spun in all directions at once.
sentences.cn: 盒子里装着一个四面八方都在转的指南针。

sentences.en: Old Helm closed the box carefully and returned it.
sentences.cn: 老舵小心地关上盒子，又把它还给了她。

sentences.en: 'We find our own way,' he told her.
sentences.cn: 他告诉她，我们自己找路。

sentences.en: She shrugged and sailed off.
sentences.cn: 她耸了耸肩，扬帆离去。

claim:2.en: A narrow stone pillar rose from the clouds with a single flag planted at its top. Silverfang circled it in her ship. 'I *claim* this marker island,' she called across to us. 'First to plant a flag, first to own the word carved on it.' Old Helm crossed his arms. He had spotted the same island an hour before her.
claim:2.cnHint: 银牙抢先插旗，____这块刻有字词的标记小岛归她所有，但老舵长对此提出了异议。
claim:2.hook: Old Helm reached into his coat and produced a flag of his own.
claim:2.line: 'I *claim* this island — my flag went up before you even left your deck.'

sentences.en: A narrow stone pillar rose from the clouds with a single flag planted at its top.
sentences.cn: 一根狭长的石柱从云层中升起，顶端插着一面旗子。

sentences.en: Silverfang circled it in her ship.
sentences.cn: 银牙在她的船上绕着它转圈。

sentences.en: 'I *claim* this marker island,' she called across to us.
'First to plant a flag, first to own the word carved on it.'
sentences.cn: 我先插的旗子，就拥有刻在上面的词。

sentences.en: Old Helm crossed his arms.
sentences.cn: 老舵交叉着双臂。

sentences.en: He had spotted the same island an hour before her.
sentences.cn: 他在她之前一小时就发现了同样的岛屿。

half:2.en: The word carved into the pillar was split down the middle — *half* on one face of the stone, the other half on the reverse side. Neither our troupe nor Silverfang's crew could read the whole word alone. Bell looked at me and lowered her voice. 'Looks like we need each other, whether we like it or not.'
half:2.cnHint: 石柱上的词语被一分为二，我们只得到了____，必须与对手合作才能读出完整的字。
half:2.hook: Silverfang's expression shifted from triumph to something almost like respect.
half:2.line: 'I can only read *half* — and I suspect your half is the more important one.'

sentences.en: The word carved into the pillar was split down the middle — *half* on one face of the stone, the other half on the reverse side.
Neither our troupe nor Silverfang's crew could read the whole word alone.
sentences.cn: 无论是我们的剧团还是银牙的船员，都无法单独读懂整个词。

sentences.en: Bell looked at me and lowered her voice.
sentences.cn: 小铃看了看我，压低了嗓音。

sentences.en: 'Looks like we need each other, whether we like it or not.'
sentences.cn: 看起来我们需要彼此，不管愿不愿意。

successful:2.en: We reunited the two halves of the word and the pillar lit up gold. The gate at the island's edge swung open with a low, warm tone. 'A *successful* trade,' Old Helm announced, and even Silverfang gave a short nod. For one quiet moment, both crews stood together watching the new horizon appear beyond the gate.
successful:2.cnHint: 两队合力破解了词语，终于____地打开了岛屿边缘的大门，迎来了新的地平线。
successful:2.hook: Beyond the gate, two paths split in opposite directions — each one calling our names.
successful:2.line: 'A *successful* partnership — do not expect me to admit that a second time.'

sentences.en: We reunited the two halves of the word and the pillar lit up gold.
sentences.cn: 我们把词的两半重新拼接起来，石柱闪烁着金光。

sentences.en: The gate at the island's edge swung open with a low, warm tone.
sentences.cn: 岛屿边缘的大门伴随着低沉温暖的音调打开了。

sentences.en: 'A *successful* trade,' Old Helm announced, and even Silverfang gave a short nod.
For one quiet moment, both crews stood together watching the new horizon appear beyond the gate.
sentences.cn: 一段时间里，两支船队肩并肩地站在一起，看着新地平线在大门那边显现。

access:2.en: The open gate should have led straight through, but a wall of thick silver mist blocked the way. Bell discovered a small panel on the gate post, with slots shaped like word-fragments. 'We need the right pieces to *access* the path,' she said, fitting our earned fragments in one by one. The mist thinned with each click.
access:2.cnHint: 大门虽然打开了，但迷雾阻挡了去路，小铃发现必须用字词碎片才能____前方的道路。
access:2.hook: The last slot was shaped like a fragment only Silverfang's crew was carrying.
access:2.line: 'We cannot *access* the next island without that final piece — and she knows it.'

sentences.en: The open gate should have led straight through, but a wall of thick silver mist blocked the way.
sentences.cn: 敞开的大门本该直通过去，但一堵厚重的银色迷雾挡住了去路。

sentences.en: Bell discovered a small panel on the gate post, with slots shaped like word-fragments.
sentences.cn: 小铃在大门的柱子上发现了一个小面板，上面有词片形状的插槽。

sentences.en: 'We need the right pieces to *access* the path,' she said, fitting our earned fragments in one by one.
The mist thinned with each click.
sentences.cn: 雾气每次点击都会变薄。

determine:2.en: Deep inside Silverfang's ship, Bell found a locked iron box bolted to the wall. She turned it over in her hands, studying every scratch and mark. 'We need to *determine* which key fits before he returns,' she whispered, her lamp throwing long shadows across the hold.
determine:2.cnHint: 小铃在银牙的船舱里发现了一个上锁的铁箱，试图在银牙回来前____出哪把钥匙能打开它。
determine:2.hook: Footsteps echoed on the deck above.
determine:2.line: 'We must *determine* the answer before that door opens.'

sentences.en: Deep inside Silverfang's ship, Bell found a locked iron box bolted to the wall.
sentences.cn: 在银牙船的深处，小铃找到了一个锁上的铁盒子，用螺栓固定在墙上。

sentences.en: She turned it over in her hands, studying every scratch and mark.
sentences.cn: 她在手里翻转着它，研究着每一道刮痕和印记。

sentences.en: 'We need to *determine* which key fits before he returns,' she whispered, her lamp throwing long shadows across the hold.

response:2.en: Old Helm sent a signal flag up the mast — three short dips, the troupe's old greeting. We waited. For a long moment, Silverfang's ship sat silent. Then, slowly, a single lantern swung port to starboard. It was a *response*, and it meant: come alone.
response:2.cnHint: 老舵长打出旗语问候，银牙的船终于给出了____，意思是：单独来。
response:2.hook: Old Helm folded the flag without saying a word.
response:2.line: 'That *response* means he is willing to talk — barely.'

sentences.en: Old Helm sent a signal flag up the mast — three short dips, the troupe's old greeting.
sentences.cn: 老舵沿着桅杆竖起了一面信号旗——三次短晃，我们剧团的老招呼方式。

sentences.en: We waited.
sentences.cn: 我们等待着。

sentences.en: For a long moment, Silverfang's ship sat silent.
sentences.cn: 有一会儿，银牙的船安静得没有一点声息。

sentences.en: Then, slowly, a single lantern swung port to starboard.
sentences.cn: 然后，缓缓地，一盏灯笼从左舷摇到右舷。

sentences.en: It was a *response*, and it meant: come alone.

search:2.en: The island's market was a tangle of bright stalls and loud voices. Bell had lost the wager token somewhere in the crowd. Our *search* took us down every narrow lane, under every canvas awning, until a small child tugged Bell's sleeve and held the token up, grinning.
search:2.cnHint: 小铃在市集上丢失了赌约信物，我们在人群中展开____，最终被一个小孩找到并归还。
search:2.hook: The token felt strangely warm in Bell's palm.
search:2.line: 'Our *search* ends here — and the real question begins.'

sentences.en: The island's market was a tangle of bright stalls and loud voices.
sentences.cn: 岛屿的集市是一片五彩斑斓的摊位和响亮的人声。

sentences.en: Bell had lost the wager token somewhere in the crowd.
sentences.cn: 小铃在人群中丢失了赌注代币。

sentences.en: Our *search* took us down every narrow lane, under every canvas awning, until a small child tugged Bell's sleeve and held the token up, grinning.

regard:2.en: When Silverfang finally stepped aboard, Old Helm did not move. He simply stood at the stern and *regarded* the captain with calm, steady eyes — the way a lighthouse watches a ship, saying nothing, missing nothing. Silverfang was the first to look away.
regard:2.cnHint: 银牙登船时，老舵长静静地____着他，目光平稳如灯塔，银牙先移开了视线。
regard:2.hook: The silence between them held an unspoken wager.
regard:2.line: 'I *regard* you as a rival, not an enemy — remember that.'

sentences.en: When Silverfang finally stepped aboard, Old Helm did not move.
sentences.cn: 当银牙终于登上船时，老舵没有动。

sentences.en: He simply stood at the stern and *regarded* the captain with calm, steady eyes — the way a lighthouse watches a ship, saying nothing, missing nothing.
Silverfang was the first to look away.
sentences.cn: 银牙最先移开了目光。

true:2.en: Silverfang spread a chart across the barrel and jabbed a finger at a blank patch of sky. 'This island exists,' he said flatly. Old Helm studied the lines, then nodded. 'If the star angles are *true*, it should be two days east.' For the first time, both men smiled.
true:2.cnHint: 银牙展示海图，老舵长确认星角数据____实可靠，两人第一次同时露出了笑容。
true:2.hook: Two days east — and something unknown waited there.
true:2.line: 'If these star readings are *true*, we sail at dawn.'

sentences.en: Silverfang spread a chart across the barrel and jabbed a finger at a blank patch of sky.
sentences.cn: 银牙在木桶上摊开了一张图，用手指戳向天空中的一片空白区域。

sentences.en: 'This island exists,' he said flatly.
sentences.cn: 她平静地说，这座岛屿存在。

sentences.en: Old Helm studied the lines, then nodded.
sentences.cn: 老舵研究了这些线条，然后点了点头。

sentences.en: 'If the star angles are *true*, it should be two days east.'
For the first time, both men smiled.
sentences.cn: 两人第一次都笑了。

depend:2.en: The wager was simple: whoever reached the Crystal Shelf first would keep both map fragments. But Bell pointed out that everything would *depend* on the wind. A fair breeze and Silverfang's wider sails would win easily. A still night and our lighter hull would slip ahead.
depend:2.cnHint: 赌约的胜负将____于风向，顺风银牙占优，无风则我们的轻船领先。
depend:2.hook: Bell looked up — the weather-flag was perfectly still.
depend:2.line: 'Victory will *depend* on the wind, and only the wind.'

sentences.en: The wager was simple: whoever reached the Crystal Shelf first would keep both map fragments.
sentences.cn: 赌注很简单：谁先到达水晶架，谁就能拿走两份地图残片。

sentences.en: But Bell pointed out that everything would *depend* on the wind.
A fair breeze and Silverfang's wider sails would win easily.
sentences.cn: 风平浪静，银牙的宽帆会轻松胜出。

sentences.en: A still night and our lighter hull would slip ahead.
sentences.cn: 静夜无风，我们轻巧的船体就能悄悄超前。

expensive:2.en: Among the goods stacked in Silverfang's hold, one crate stood apart: sealed with blue wax and marked with no name. 'Don't touch that,' Silverfang said quietly. 'Very *expensive* — and not mine to sell.' He slid it behind a rope coil, but Bell had already memorised its shape.
expensive:2.cnHint: 银牙船舱里有一只封着蓝蜡的神秘箱子，他说那东西非常____，而且不属于他，但小铃已经悄悄记住了它的形状。
expensive:2.hook: Bell sketched the wax seal from memory that night.
expensive:2.line: 'That crate is *expensive* — and worth far more than coin.'

sentences.en: Among the goods stacked in Silverfang's hold, one crate stood apart: sealed with blue wax and marked with no name.
sentences.cn: 银牙船舱里堆放的货物中，有一只木箱格外特殊：用蓝色封漆封好，上面没有任何标记。

sentences.en: 'Don't touch that,' Silverfang said quietly.
sentences.cn: "别碰那个，"银牙轻声说。

sentences.en: 'Very *expensive* — and not mine to sell.'
He slid it behind a rope coil, but Bell had already memorised its shape.
sentences.cn: 他把它塞到一圈绳子后面，但小铃早已把它的形状烙在心里。

explain:2.en: A rolled note fell from the beak of a silver bird at my feet. Old Helm unfolded it slowly. 'Silverfang wants a wager,' he said. I asked him to *explain*, and he spread the paper flat on the barrel so we could all read the thin, careful words.
explain:2.cnHint: 一张纸条从鸟嘴里落下，老舵带着我们一起____它的内容。
explain:2.hook: The last line of the note made Old Helm go very still.
explain:2.line: 'Let me *explain* the terms before anyone agrees to anything.'

sentences.en: A rolled note fell from the beak of a silver bird at my feet.
sentences.cn: 一只银色鸟儿从它的喙里掉下一卷纸条，落在我脚边。

sentences.en: Old Helm unfolded it slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢展开它。

sentences.en: 'Silverfang wants a wager,' he said.
sentences.cn: "银牙想跟我们赌一局，"他说。

sentences.en: I asked him to *explain*, and he spread the paper flat on the barrel so we could all read the thin, careful words.

examine:2.en: Bell found the object wedged between two stones near the anchor rope: a small glass lens, cloudy with age. She held it to the starlight and began to *examine* every edge, turning it slowly, breathing on it, wiping it clean with the corner of her scarf.
examine:2.cnHint: 小铃在锚绳旁发现了一块旧玻璃镜片，仔细____它的每一处边缘。
examine:2.hook: One edge was not glass at all — it was a door.
examine:2.line: 'I need to *examine* this before we hand it over to Silverfang.'

sentences.en: Bell found the object wedged between two stones near the anchor rope: a small glass lens, cloudy with age.
sentences.cn: 小铃在靠近锚绳的两块石头间找到了那样东西：一只小玻璃透镜，被岁月染得浑浊。

sentences.en: She held it to the starlight and began to *examine* every edge, turning it slowly, breathing on it, wiping it clean with the corner of her scarf.

influence:2.en: Old Helm warned us that Silverfang had friends on every island between here and the far ridge. 'His coins and his reputation *influence* every merchant and gatekeeper along the route,' he said, tapping the map. 'We cannot simply sail past and expect a warm welcome.'
influence:2.cnHint: 老舵提醒我们，银牙的财富和名声____着沿途每一个岛屿上的人。
influence:2.hook: Then Bell pointed to a gap in the map no coin could buy.
influence:2.line: 'His reputation can *influence* people we have not even met yet.'

sentences.en: Old Helm warned us that Silverfang had friends on every island between here and the far ridge.
sentences.cn: 老舵警告我们，银牙在这里到远山脊之间的每座岛屿上都有朋友。

sentences.en: 'His coins and his reputation *influence* every merchant and gatekeeper along the route,' he said, tapping the map.
'We cannot simply sail past and expect a warm welcome.'
sentences.cn: "我们不能就这样扬帆驶过，还指望受到热烈欢迎。"

argue:2.en: Silverfang's messenger waited on the rope bridge, arms folded. Old Helm and I began to *argue* about whether to accept the wager at all — our voices low but sharp, the bridge swaying gently under us, the messenger watching with calm, patient eyes.
argue:2.cnHint: 老舵和我站在绳桥上，为是否接受赌约而____，声音压低却针锋相对。
argue:2.hook: The messenger smiled, as if our argument was exactly what he had expected.
argue:2.line: 'I will *argue* our side — just give me one moment to think.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's messenger waited on the rope bridge, arms folded.
sentences.cn: 银牙的信使站在绳桥上，双臂交叉在胸前。

sentences.en: Old Helm and I began to *argue* about whether to accept the wager at all — our voices low but sharp, the bridge swaying gently under us, the messenger watching with calm, patient eyes.

pass:2.en: The messenger asked us to *pass* a sealed token to Silverfang by sunrise — no opening it, no delay. Old Helm placed it in my hands as if it weighed more than stone. I slipped it into my coat pocket and nodded without a word.
pass:2.cnHint: 信使要求我们在日出前将一枚封好的令牌____给银牙，不得拆开。
pass:2.hook: Something inside the token ticked, soft and steady, like a tiny heart.
pass:2.line: '*Pass* it to him directly — do not let anyone else touch it.'

sentences.en: The messenger asked us to *pass* a sealed token to Silverfang by sunrise — no opening it, no delay.
Old Helm placed it in my hands as if it weighed more than stone.
sentences.cn: 老舵把它放在我手里，仿佛它的重量超过了石头。

sentences.en: I slipped it into my coat pocket and nodded without a word.
sentences.cn: 我把它塞进外套口袋，无言地点了点头。

serious:2.en: Back on deck, Bell spread the wager terms across the table. Old Helm read them twice, said nothing, then read them a third time. His face, usually open and warm, became *serious* in a way I had never seen before — the kind of serious that means real danger ahead.
serious:2.cnHint: 老舵读完赌约条款后，神情变得前所未有的____，那种表情意味着真正的危险。
serious:2.hook: He folded the paper and asked Bell to hide it below deck.
serious:2.line: 'This is *serious* — Silverfang does not write terms like these for fun.'

sentences.en: Back on deck, Bell spread the wager terms across the table.
sentences.cn: 回到甲板上，小铃把赌约条款铺在桌子上。

sentences.en: Old Helm read them twice, said nothing, then read them a third time.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍，什么也没说，然后又读了第三遍。

sentences.en: His face, usually open and warm, became *serious* in a way I had never seen before — the kind of serious that means real danger ahead.

despite:2.en: *Despite* the thick cloud rolling in from the east, Bell steered us toward the signal lantern blinking on the far platform. The wind pushed hard against the hull. We leaned into the railing and watched the light grow slowly, stubbornly brighter through the grey.
despite:2.cnHint: ____乌云从东边涌来，小铃仍坚定地驶向远处平台上闪烁的信号灯。
despite:2.hook: The lantern blinked once more, then stopped — and a shape stepped out of the dark.
despite:2.line: 'We press on *despite* the weather — that light is meant for us.'

sentences.en: *Despite* the thick cloud rolling in from the east, Bell steered us toward the signal lantern blinking on the far platform.
The wind pushed hard against the hull.
sentences.cn: 风猛烈地冲撞着船体。

sentences.en: We leaned into the railing and watched the light grow slowly, stubbornly brighter through the grey.
sentences.cn: 我们靠在栏杆上，看着那盏灯光穿过灰蒙蒙的雾气，缓缓、顽强地越来越亮。

express:2.en: Old Helm rarely shows much feeling, so when he gripped my shoulder and looked me in the eye, I paid close attention. He did not *express* it in many words — just three: 'trust your feet.' Then he stepped back and let me walk toward Silverfang alone.
express:2.cnHint: 老舵很少流露情感，这次他只用了三个字来____他想说的话，然后让我独自前行。
express:2.hook: Silverfang was already watching me from the far end of the bridge.
express:2.line: 'I find it hard to *express* how much this wager matters to all of us.'

sentences.en: Old Helm rarely shows much feeling, so when he gripped my shoulder and looked me in the eye, I paid close attention.
sentences.cn: 老舵很少流露感情，所以当他抓住我的肩膀，眼睛对着我看时，我认真地听了。

sentences.en: He did not *express* it in many words — just three: 'trust your feet.'
Then he stepped back and let me walk toward Silverfang alone.
sentences.cn: 然后他退后一步，让我独自走向银牙。

conduct:2.en: A sealed letter was pinned to the mast of Silverfang's ship. Old Helm read it aloud, his voice careful and slow. The letter judged our troupe's *conduct* on the last island — every choice recorded, every step noted. Silverfang had been watching us far longer than we knew.
conduct:2.cnHint: 银牙的信评价了我们在上一座岛上的____，老舵读信时神情凝重。
conduct:2.hook: Every step we had taken was already in his hands.
conduct:2.line: 'Your *conduct* on that island tells me everything I need to know.'

sentences.en: A sealed letter was pinned to the mast of Silverfang's ship.
sentences.cn: 银牙的船桅上钉着一封密封的信。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it aloud, his voice careful and slow.
sentences.cn: 老舵大声读出来，声音谨慎而缓慢。

sentences.en: The letter judged our troupe's *conduct* on the last island — every choice recorded, every step noted.
Silverfang had been watching us far longer than we knew.
sentences.cn: 银牙一直在监视我们，远比我们想象的要久。

reveal:2.en: Inside an old brass box found near the docking post, there was a folded map. When Bell pressed the hidden clasp, the map began to *reveal* a second layer beneath the first — a secret route drawn in silver ink. No one in the troupe had seen it before.
reveal:2.cnHint: 小铃打开铜盒，地图慢慢____出一条用银色墨水画成的隐秘航线。
reveal:2.hook: The silver path led somewhere none of our charts had ever shown.
reveal:2.line: 'It will *reveal* a road that Silverfang thinks only he knows.'

sentences.en: Inside an old brass box found near the docking post, there was a folded map.
sentences.cn: 在停泊柱附近找到的一个古老黄铜盒里，有一份折起来的地图。

sentences.en: When Bell pressed the hidden clasp, the map began to *reveal* a second layer beneath the first — a secret route drawn in silver ink.
No one in the troupe had seen it before.
sentences.cn: 船队里没人见过它。

powerful:2.en: The wind instrument mounted on Silverfang's ship was unlike anything we carried. Bell stared at it for a long moment. 'That device is *powerful* enough to read the air three islands ahead,' she said quietly. Our own tools suddenly felt small and old beside it.
powerful:2.cnHint: 小铃发现银牙船上的风力仪器极为____，能探测三座岛屿之外的气流。
powerful:2.hook: With that device, he would always arrive before us.
powerful:2.line: 'It is the most *powerful* instrument I have ever seen on any ship.'

sentences.en: The wind instrument mounted on Silverfang's ship was unlike anything we carried.
sentences.cn: 银牙船上安装的风力乐器跟我们带的任何东西都不一样。

sentences.en: Bell stared at it for a long moment.
sentences.cn: 小铃盯着它看了很久。

sentences.en: 'That device is *powerful* enough to read the air three islands ahead,' she said quietly.
Our own tools suddenly felt small and old beside it.
sentences.cn: 我们自己的工具在它面前突然显得又小又旧。

push:2.en: Old Helm spread the recovered map across the table and tapped a narrow passage between two storm clouds. 'This is the *push* we need,' he said firmly. If we moved now, before Silverfang resupplied, we could reach the word-island first and claim its fragment.
push:2.cnHint: 老舵指着地图上的险道说，这是我们需要的____，必须趁银牙补给前出发。
push:2.hook: One narrow gap, one chance — and the clock was already turning.
push:2.line: 'This *push* has to happen tonight, while the clouds are still apart.'

sentences.en: Old Helm spread the recovered map across the table and tapped a narrow passage between two storm clouds.
sentences.cn: 老舵把找到的地图铺在桌子上，指了指两团风暴云之间的狭窄通道。

sentences.en: 'This is the *push* we need,' he said firmly.
If we moved now, before Silverfang resupplied, we could reach the word-island first and claim its fragment.
sentences.cn: 如果我们现在就动身，在银牙补给之前，我们就能抢先到达那座文字岛，拿到它的碎片。

wonder:2.en: Tucked inside the brass box with the map was a small glass globe. It held a tiny floating island inside, slowly turning. Bell lifted it to the light with wide eyes. The *wonder* on her face said more than words could — none of us had ever seen anything like it.
wonder:2.cnHint: 小铃举起玻璃球，脸上满是____，那里面竟悬浮着一座微缩的小岛，缓缓旋转。
wonder:2.hook: Whatever island it showed, we needed to find it.
wonder:2.line: 'The *wonder* of it — a whole island living inside a piece of glass.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside the brass box with the map was a small glass globe.
sentences.cn: 装地图的黄铜盒子里还藏着一个小玻璃球。

sentences.en: It held a tiny floating island inside, slowly turning.
sentences.cn: 里面漂浮着一座微型岛屿，缓缓转动。

sentences.en: Bell lifted it to the light with wide eyes.
sentences.cn: 小铃把它举向光线，眼睛睁得很大。

sentences.en: The *wonder* on her face said more than words could — none of us had ever seen anything like it.

design:2.en: Bell spent an hour at the table with paper and charcoal. She had chosen to *design* a new signal flag — one that would look like Silverfang's colours from a distance but carry a hidden mark only our troupe could read. It was clever, quiet, and just a little risky.
design:2.cnHint: 小铃着手____一面新旗帜，远看像银牙的旗，近看却藏着只有我们认识的暗号。
design:2.hook: A false flag was only useful until someone looked too closely.
design:2.line: 'I will *design* it so even his crew will not notice the difference.'

sentences.en: Bell spent an hour at the table with paper and charcoal.
sentences.cn: 小铃在桌前花了一小时，用纸和木炭。

sentences.en: She had chosen to *design* a new signal flag — one that would look like Silverfang's colours from a distance but carry a hidden mark only our troupe could read.
It was clever, quiet, and just a little risky.
sentences.cn: 这个主意既聪明又低调，还有点冒险。

exercise:2.en: Every morning on the upper deck, Bell would *exercise* with a short wooden rod, moving through slow, precise forms. Old Helm watched from the railing one morning and said nothing. But after breakfast he quietly asked her to teach the rest of us. We started that same afternoon.
exercise:2.cnHint: 小铃每天早晨在甲板上用木棍____，老舵看完后请她教大家，当天下午就开始了。
exercise:2.hook: Old Helm never asked for anything without a reason.
exercise:2.line: 'If we *exercise* together each morning, we move better as a troupe.'

sentences.en: Every morning on the upper deck, Bell would *exercise* with a short wooden rod, moving through slow, precise forms.
Old Helm watched from the railing one morning and said nothing.
sentences.cn: 一个早晨，老舵从栏杆边看着，什么也没说。

sentences.en: But after breakfast he quietly asked her to teach the rest of us.
sentences.cn: 但吃完早餐后，他悄悄问她能不能教我们其他人。

sentences.en: We started that same afternoon.
sentences.cn: 那天下午我们就开始了。

space:2.en: The message from Silverfang was brief: he would meet us at the next island, not to fight, but to talk. Old Helm folded the note and looked out at the open sky. 'Give me some *space* to think,' he said. The troupe stepped back, and the silence grew wide around him.
space:2.cnHint: 看完银牙的信，老舵说需要一些____来思考，众人默默退开，甲板上安静下来。
space:2.hook: Whatever he decided next would change the shape of the bet entirely.
space:2.line: 'I just need a little *space* — this choice is not a small one.'

sentences.en: The message from Silverfang was brief: he would meet us at the next island, not to fight, but to talk.
sentences.cn: 银牙的消息很简短：他会在下一座岛屿见我们，不是来打架，而是来谈话。

sentences.en: Old Helm folded the note and looked out at the open sky.
sentences.cn: 老舵折好纸条，望向开阔的天空。

sentences.en: 'Give me some *space* to think,' he said.
The troupe stepped back, and the silence grew wide around him.
sentences.cn: 船队退开了，寂静在他周围蔓延开来。

real:2.en: Inside Silverfang's locked chest, tucked beneath a folded map, I found a small glass globe. Inside it, a tiny island floated in slow circles. Old Helm leaned close and whispered that the globe showed only *real* places — islands that existed somewhere above us, waiting to be reached.
real:2.cnHint: 在银牙的箱子里，我们发现了一个玻璃球，老舵说它只显示____的地方。
real:2.hook: The island inside the globe began to spin faster.
real:2.line: 'Every island in that globe is *real* — I have stood on each one.'

sentences.en: Inside Silverfang's locked chest, tucked beneath a folded map, I found a small glass globe.
sentences.cn: 在银牙上了锁的箱子里，折起的地图下面，我发现了一个小玻璃球。

sentences.en: Inside it, a tiny island floated in slow circles.
sentences.cn: 里面有座微型岛屿在缓缓盘旋。

sentences.en: Old Helm leaned close and whispered that the globe showed only *real* places — islands that existed somewhere above us, waiting to be reached.

talk:2.en: Bell called us together on the deck just before dawn. She had heard something odd during the night: voices carried on the wind from the island below. 'That kind of *talk* does not come from any crew I know,' she said, holding her lantern high and scanning the dark trees.
talk:2.cnHint: 贝尔听到了风中传来的奇怪____，把大家召集到甲板上。
talk:2.hook: A second voice answered from somewhere much closer.
talk:2.line: 'That kind of *talk* only means one thing — someone wants to be found.'

sentences.en: Bell called us together on the deck just before dawn.
sentences.cn: 天亮前，小铃把我们召集到甲板上。

sentences.en: She had heard something odd during the night: voices carried on the wind from the island below.
sentences.cn: 她在夜里听到了什么奇怪的声音：风吹过岛屿时传来的说话声。

sentences.en: 'That kind of *talk* does not come from any crew I know,' she said, holding her lantern high and scanning the dark trees.

energy:2.en: The word-fragment we had just collected glowed softly in my palm. Old Helm explained that every word held *energy* stored from the moment it was first spoken aloud. 'When the troupe reads it together,' he said, 'that stored force opens the next passage in the sky-map.'
energy:2.cnHint: 老舵解释说，每个词语碎片都储存着____，集体朗读时才能开启下一段路途。
energy:2.hook: The fragment in my hand suddenly grew very warm.
energy:2.line: 'A word holds more *energy* than any engine I have ever seen.'

sentences.en: The word-fragment we had just collected glowed softly in my palm.
sentences.cn: 我刚收集到的文字碎片在掌心里微微发光。

sentences.en: Old Helm explained that every word held *energy* stored from the moment it was first spoken aloud.
'When the troupe reads it together,' he said, 'that stored force opens the next passage in the sky-map.'
sentences.cn: "当船队一起读它时，"他说，"那股储存的力量就能打开天空地图里的下一条通道。"

plan:2.en: Silverfang's messenger bird landed on our railing with a small note tied to its leg. The note held a single sentence: meet at the Amber Dock before the third bell. Old Helm read it twice, then smiled. 'This changes our *plan*,' he said, rolling the sky-map back up carefully.
plan:2.cnHint: 银牙的信鸟带来一张纸条，老舵说这改变了我们的____。
plan:2.hook: Old Helm did not say what the new plan would be.
plan:2.line: 'A message like this changes every *plan* we made last night.'

sentences.en: Silverfang's messenger bird landed on our railing with a small note tied to its leg.
sentences.cn: 银牙的信鸽降落在我们的栏杆上，腿上绑着一张小纸条。

sentences.en: The note held a single sentence: meet at the Amber Dock before the third bell.
sentences.cn: 纸条上只有一句话：在第三声钟声前在琥珀码头见。

sentences.en: Old Helm read it twice, then smiled.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍，然后笑了。

sentences.en: 'This changes our *plan*,' he said, rolling the sky-map back up carefully.

bear:2.en: At the centre of the Amber Dock stood an old stone pillar. Carved into it were dozens of words, each one worn smooth by years of wind. Bell ran her fingers across the surface. 'These pillars *bear* the names of every troupe that ever passed through,' she said quietly. 'We should add ours.'
bear:2.cnHint: 琥珀码头的石柱____着所有曾经到访的队伍的名字，贝尔建议我们也刻上自己的。
bear:2.hook: One name near the bottom had been freshly scratched out.
bear:2.line: 'These old stones *bear* more history than any book I have read.'

sentences.en: At the centre of the Amber Dock stood an old stone pillar.
sentences.cn: 琥珀码头的中央竖立着一根古老的石柱。

sentences.en: Carved into it were dozens of words, each one worn smooth by years of wind.
sentences.cn: 柱子上刻满了几十个词，每一个都被多年的风吹得光滑。

sentences.en: Bell ran her fingers across the surface.
sentences.cn: 小铃用手指划过表面。

sentences.en: 'These pillars *bear* the names of every troupe that ever passed through,' she said quietly.
'We should add ours.'
sentences.cn: "我们应该加上自己的。"

organization:2.en: Tucked inside the pillar's hollow base was a folded sheet listing rules and a symbol I did not recognise. Old Helm identified it at once: the mark of the Sky Accord, an *organization* that once governed safe passage between all the floating islands. 'They have been silent for thirty years,' he murmured.
organization:2.cnHint: 石柱底部藏着一份文件，属于一个曾管理浮岛通行权的____，已沉寂三十年。
organization:2.hook: The seal on the sheet was still warm to the touch.
organization:2.line: 'The Sky Accord was the oldest *organization* these islands ever knew.'

sentences.en: Tucked inside the pillar's hollow base was a folded sheet listing rules and a symbol I did not recognise.
sentences.cn: 柱子底部的空心处折着一张纸，上面列着一些规则和一个我不认识的符号。

sentences.en: Old Helm identified it at once: the mark of the Sky Accord, an *organization* that once governed safe passage between all the floating islands.
'They have been silent for thirty years,' he murmured.
sentences.cn: "三十年来他们一直沉默不语，"他低声说。

opportunity:2.en: Silverfang arrived at the dock just as the third bell rang. He spread a new chart on the barrel between us and tapped a blank region near the eastern edge. 'That blank space is an *opportunity*,' he said with a grin. 'First troupe to name it claims the passage rights through it forever.'
opportunity:2.cnHint: 银牙向大家展示地图上的空白区域，说那片空白是一个____，最先命名的队伍将永久拥有通行权。
opportunity:2.hook: Old Helm's eyes moved to our word-fragments without a word.
opportunity:2.line: 'An empty space on any map is always an *opportunity*, never a problem.'

sentences.en: Silverfang arrived at the dock just as the third bell rang.
sentences.cn: 银牙到达码头时，第三声钟声正好响起。

sentences.en: He spread a new chart on the barrel between us and tapped a blank region near the eastern edge.
sentences.cn: 他在我们之间的木桶上铺开一张新地图，敲了敲靠近东边边缘的一片空白区域。

sentences.en: 'That blank space is an *opportunity*,' he said with a grin.
'First troupe to name it claims the passage rights through it forever.'
sentences.cn: 第一支队伍给它命名就永远拥有通过它的通道权。

professor:2.en: Among Silverfang's crew stood a quiet figure in a patched coat, holding a thick notebook. Silverfang introduced her as a *professor* from the Island Academy, brought along to verify that any newly named region followed the ancient rules of sky-cartography. She bowed slightly and said nothing, but her pen was already open.
professor:2.cnHint: 银牙的船队里有一位来自岛屿学院的____，负责核实新命名区域是否符合古老的天空制图规则。
professor:2.hook: She had already written our troupe's name in her notebook.
professor:2.line: 'A *professor* of sky-maps sees things the rest of us walk right past.'

sentences.en: Among Silverfang's crew stood a quiet figure in a patched coat, holding a thick notebook.
sentences.cn: 在银牙的船员中站着一个穿着打补丁外套的安静身影，拿着一本厚重的笔记本。

sentences.en: Silverfang introduced her as a *professor* from the Island Academy, brought along to verify that any newly named region followed the ancient rules of sky-cartography.
She bowed slightly and said nothing, but her pen was already open.
sentences.cn: 她微微鞠了一躬，什么都没说，但她的笔已经打开了。

sign:2.en: Bell found it first: a carved arrow on the bark of a giant cloud-tree, pointing toward the eastern edge of the island. 'That's a *sign*,' she said, brushing moss from its edges. Old Helm knelt beside her, studying the symbol with quiet care. Someone had passed this way before us.
sign:2.cnHint: 小铃在云树上发现了一个刻出的____，指向岛屿东边。
sign:2.hook: But the carving was still fresh, the wood still warm.
sign:2.line: 'Every *sign* points somewhere — we just have to be brave enough to follow.'

sentences.en: Bell found it first: a carved arrow on the bark of a giant cloud-tree, pointing toward the eastern edge of the island.
sentences.cn: 小铃先发现的：一根巨大云树的树皮上刻着一支箭，指向岛屿东边的边缘。

sentences.en: 'That's a *sign*,' she said, brushing moss from its edges.
Old Helm knelt beside her, studying the symbol with quiet care.
sentences.cn: 老舵在她身旁跪下，用心研究着那个符号。

sentences.en: Someone had passed this way before us.
sentences.cn: 有人在我们之前经过过这里。

feeling:2.en: I stepped onto the narrow rope bridge between two floating rocks, and a strange *feeling* rose in my chest — not fear exactly, but a kind of buzzing alertness. Old Helm had warned me about this bridge. The air tasted of copper, and the stars below us seemed closer than the ones above.
feeling:2.cnHint: 踏上浮岛间的绳桥时，叙述者心中涌起一种奇特的____。
feeling:2.hook: Then the bridge began to hum, very softly, all on its own.
feeling:2.line: 'Trust that *feeling* — it means the island is trying to tell you something.'

sentences.en: I stepped onto the narrow rope bridge between two floating rocks, and a strange *feeling* rose in my chest — not fear exactly, but a kind of buzzing alertness.
Old Helm had warned me about this bridge.
sentences.cn: 老舵曾经警告过我关于这座桥。

sentences.en: The air tasted of copper, and the stars below us seemed closer than the ones above.
sentences.cn: 空气尝起来有铜的味道，我们下方的星星似乎比上方的更近。

professional:2.en: Silverfang spread the old map across a barrel and studied it with sharp, steady eyes. His hands never shook. 'He moves like a *professional*,' Bell whispered to me. Old Helm only nodded. Whatever Silverfang was searching for on that map, he had clearly spent years learning exactly how to find it.
professional:2.cnHint: 小铃悄悄告诉叙述者，银牙看地图的样子像个真正的____。
professional:2.hook: Silverfang circled one small island and said nothing at all.
professional:2.line: 'A *professional* never marks the map until he is certain.'

sentences.en: Silverfang spread the old map across a barrel and studied it with sharp, steady eyes.
sentences.cn: 银牙把旧地图铺在木桶上，用锐利而沉着的眼睛研究着。

sentences.en: His hands never shook.
sentences.cn: 他的手从不颤抖。

sentences.en: 'He moves like a *professional*,' Bell whispered to me.
Old Helm only nodded.
sentences.cn: 老舵只是点了点头。

sentences.en: Whatever Silverfang was searching for on that map, he had clearly spent years learning exactly how to find it.
sentences.cn: 不管银牙在地图上寻找什么，他显然花了多年时间来学习确切该怎么找到它。

behind:2.en: We drifted through a canyon of pale stone pillars, and I noticed our rival ship was no longer visible on the horizon. 'We left them *behind*,' I said, surprised. Bell checked the compass twice. Old Helm smiled, but it was a careful smile — the kind that held more worry than joy. Distance on these islands was never simple.
behind:2.cnHint: 叙述者发现银牙的船已经____我们，不见踪影了。
behind:2.hook: Then Old Helm pointed upward — the rival ship was above us.
behind:2.line: 'Being *behind* once taught me more than winning ever did.'

sentences.en: We drifted through a canyon of pale stone pillars, and I noticed our rival ship was no longer visible on the horizon.
sentences.cn: 我们飘过一个淡色石柱的峡谷，我注意到我们的对手船已经不在地平线上了。

sentences.en: 'We left them *behind*,' I said, surprised.
Bell checked the compass twice.
sentences.cn: 小铃检查了两次指南针。

sentences.en: Old Helm smiled, but it was a careful smile — the kind that held more worry than joy.
sentences.cn: 老舵笑了，但那是一个谨慎的笑——那种包含更多担忧而非欢乐的笑。

sentences.en: Distance on these islands was never simple.
sentences.cn: 这些岛屿上的距离从不简单。

government:2.en: Inside the hollow tower, stone tablets lined every wall. Bell read one aloud: a record of the island council — the old *government* of the sky peoples, dissolved a hundred years ago. Their last law, carved in deep letters, was a single sentence: no island shall be sold, only shared. Old Helm touched the words gently.
government:2.cnHint: 空塔里的石碑记录着百年前天空岛民的____留下的最后法令。
government:2.hook: Below the law, someone had added a new name in fresh ink.
government:2.line: 'Even a broken *government* leaves words behind — and words remember.'

sentences.en: Inside the hollow tower, stone tablets lined every wall.
sentences.cn: 在空心塔内，石板排列在每面墙上。

sentences.en: Bell read one aloud: a record of the island council — the old *government* of the sky peoples, dissolved a hundred years ago.
Their last law, carved in deep letters, was a single sentence: no island shall be sold, only shared.
sentences.cn: 他们的最后一条法律，用深深的字刻着，是一个单句：没有岛屿应该被出售，只能被共享。

sentences.en: Old Helm touched the words gently.
sentences.cn: 老舵轻轻地触摸了那些字。

growth:2.en: At the centre of the island stood a tree unlike any other: its roots floated free of the soil, and its rings glowed faintly gold in the starlight. Bell called it a *growth* map — each ring marked a year the sky islands had expanded outward. Old Helm counted the rings in silence. There were far more than expected.
growth:2.cnHint: 小铃说那棵树发光的年轮记录着浮空岛的____历史。
growth:2.hook: The outermost ring was still forming, right before our eyes.
growth:2.line: 'Real *growth* leaves a mark you can count on long after.'

sentences.en: At the centre of the island stood a tree unlike any other: its roots floated free of the soil, and its rings glowed faintly gold in the starlight.
sentences.cn: 在岛屿中央站着一棵与众不同的树：它的根浮在土壤外，它的年轮在星光下发出微弱的金光。

sentences.en: Bell called it a *growth* map — each ring marked a year the sky islands had expanded outward.
Old Helm counted the rings in silence.
sentences.cn: 老舵沉默地数着年轮。

sentences.en: There were far more than expected.
sentences.cn: 比预期的要多得多。

negative:2.en: Silverfang slid a printed notice across the table toward Old Helm. The word at the top read: RESULT — *NEGATIVE*. It meant the island council had refused our troupe's request to cross the restricted zone. Old Helm folded the paper slowly. Bell watched him, waiting. The sky outside had turned a deep, unhelpful grey.
negative:2.cnHint: 岛屿议会的回复是____的，我们越境的申请被拒绝了。
negative:2.hook: Old Helm smiled and said, 'Good — now we try the back door.'
negative:2.line: 'A *negative* answer is just a door that opens the other way.'

sentences.en: Silverfang slid a printed notice across the table toward Old Helm.
sentences.cn: 银牙把一份印刷的通知单滑过桌子递给老舵。

sentences.en: The word at the top read: RESULT — *NEGATIVE*.
It meant the island council had refused our troupe's request to cross the restricted zone.
sentences.cn: 这意味着岛屿委员会拒绝了我们船队穿过禁区的请求。

sentences.en: Old Helm folded the paper slowly.
sentences.cn: 老舵慢慢折叠了纸张。

sentences.en: Bell watched him, waiting.
sentences.cn: 小铃看着他，等待着。

sentences.en: The sky outside had turned a deep, unhelpful grey.
sentences.cn: 窗外的天空已经变成了一种深深的、没有用的灰色。

potential:2.en: Bell unrolled a chart showing three unexplored islands to the north. She tapped the middle one, barely larger than a cloud. 'This one has *potential*,' she said. Old Helm leaned in. There was a faint word-mark at its edge — the kind that meant hidden paths, hidden rooms, hidden things waiting for whoever arrived first.
potential:2.cnHint: 小铃在航海图上指出一座小岛，说它有巨大的____。
potential:2.hook: The word-mark on the chart pulsed once, then went still.
potential:2.line: 'I always bet on *potential* — it costs nothing and pays everything.'

sentences.en: Bell unrolled a chart showing three unexplored islands to the north.
sentences.cn: 小铃展开了一张显示三个北方未探索岛屿的地图。

sentences.en: She tapped the middle one, barely larger than a cloud.
sentences.cn: 她敲了敲中间的那个，几乎不比一朵云大。

sentences.en: 'This one has *potential*,' she said.
Old Helm leaned in.
sentences.cn: 老舵靠了进去。

sentences.en: There was a faint word-mark at its edge — the kind that meant hidden paths, hidden rooms, hidden things waiting for whoever arrived first.
sentences.cn: 在它的边缘有一个淡淡的文字标记——那种意味着隐藏路径、隐藏房间、为先到达者等待的隐藏事物的标记。

career:2.en: Inside a hollow cloud-boulder, we found a small leather book. Each page listed a captain's name, the routes they had sailed, and the years they had served. Old Helm ran a finger down the list. 'Silverfang's *career* began here,' he said softly, 'on this very island, before the rivalry.'
career:2.cnHint: 我们在空心云石里发现了一本记录船长们航行生涯的旧册子，老舵意味深长地翻阅着。
career:2.hook: The last entry in the book was dated only yesterday.
career:2.line: 'A *career* like Silverfang's does not start with luck,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Inside a hollow cloud-boulder, we found a small leather book.
sentences.cn: 在一个空心云石块内，我们发现了一本小皮革书。

sentences.en: Each page listed a captain's name, the routes they had sailed, and the years they had served.
sentences.cn: 每一页都列出了一位船长的名字、他们航行过的路线以及他们服役的年份。

sentences.en: Old Helm ran a finger down the list.
sentences.cn: 老舵用手指沿着列表往下滑动。

sentences.en: 'Silverfang's *career* began here,' he said softly, 'on this very island, before the rivalry.'

medium:2.en: Bell discovered a cracked speaking-globe wedged between two moss-covered stones. She explained that the troupe once used it as a *medium* to send voice-messages across the islands. When she breathed on the glass, faint words from an old conversation stirred inside like smoke, and we all leaned in.
medium:2.cnHint: 贝尔找到一个破裂的传声球，它曾是各岛之间传递消息的____，球内似乎还留着旧声音。
medium:2.hook: The voice inside the globe sounded exactly like Silverfang.
medium:2.line: 'This globe is our only *medium* — handle it gently,' Bell warned.

sentences.en: Bell discovered a cracked speaking-globe wedged between two moss-covered stones.
sentences.cn: 小铃发现了一个卡在两块长满苔藓的石头之间的破裂的说话球。

sentences.en: She explained that the troupe once used it as a *medium* to send voice-messages across the islands.
When she breathed on the glass, faint words from an old conversation stirred inside like smoke, and we all leaned in.
sentences.cn: 当她吹向玻璃时，一段旧对话中的淡淡字词在里面像烟雾一样翻腾，我们都靠了进去。

office:2.en: At the edge of a tilted island, a small stone cabin bore a sign reading HARBOUR MASTER. Old Helm called it Silverfang's first *office*. Inside, a desk was covered with tide charts and unpaid toll receipts, all stamped with Silverfang's personal seal — a wolf biting a compass rose.
office:2.cnHint: 我们找到了银牙最初担任港务长时用过的____，桌上满是盖着他印章的旧文件。
office:2.hook: One receipt was signed with a name none of us recognised.
office:2.line: 'Every captain needs a first *office*, however small,' Old Helm said quietly.

sentences.en: At the edge of a tilted island, a small stone cabin bore a sign reading HARBOUR MASTER.
sentences.cn: 在一座倾斜的岛屿边缘，一座小石屋的招牌上写着"港务长"。

sentences.en: Old Helm called it Silverfang's first *office*.
Inside, a desk was covered with tide charts and unpaid toll receipts, all stamped with Silverfang's personal seal — a wolf biting a compass rose.
sentences.cn: 屋里，桌子上堆满了潮汐图表和未缴的通行费收据，全都盖着银牙的私人印章——一只狼咬着罗盘玫瑰。

culture:2.en: A wide plaza on the island of Cerath was lined with carvings that told the history of its sky-sailors. Bell read the descriptions aloud. The *culture* here, she explained, treated the wind as a living elder deserving respect. No ship left harbour without a song offered to the open sky.
culture:2.cnHint: 在瑟拉斯岛的广场上，贝尔为我们讲解当地独特的____——这里的人把风视为长者，出航前必须唱歌致敬。
culture:2.hook: Silverfang's ship had left this harbour without singing, it was said.
culture:2.line: 'You cannot ignore the local *culture* and expect safe winds,' Bell said.

sentences.en: A wide plaza on the island of Cerath was lined with carvings that told the history of its sky-sailors.
sentences.cn: 塞拉斯岛上宽阔的广场，两侧镌刻着讲述这座岛屿天空航海手历史的雕像。

sentences.en: Bell read the descriptions aloud.
sentences.cn: 小铃大声朗读这些描述。

sentences.en: The *culture* here, she explained, treated the wind as a living elder deserving respect.
No ship left harbour without a song offered to the open sky.
sentences.cn: 没有船能不向开阔的天空献唱就离开港口。

college:2.en: Tucked inside a brass message-tube, we found an old invitation card. It welcomed a young navigator named Silverfang to the *college* of Starchart, an island academy where pilots learned to read the living maps of the sky. Old Helm stared at it for a long moment before tucking it away.
college:2.cnHint: 一支铜制信筒里藏着一张入学邀请函，年轻的银牙曾被邀请进入星图____学习航行。
college:2.hook: Starchart college had been destroyed seven years ago, and no one knew why.
college:2.line: 'The *college* of Starchart trained the finest pilots alive,' Old Helm murmured.

sentences.en: Tucked inside a brass message-tube, we found an old invitation card.
sentences.cn: 我们在一根黄铜信筒里找到了一张老邀请函。

sentences.en: It welcomed a young navigator named Silverfang to the *college* of Starchart, an island academy where pilots learned to read the living maps of the sky.
Old Helm stared at it for a long moment before tucking it away.
sentences.cn: 老舵盯着它看了很久，然后把它收了起来。

value:2.en: Among the scattered cargo of a grounded sky-barge, Bell lifted a small jar of glowing amber dust. She held it to the starlight. 'The real *value* of this,' she said, 'is not what it sells for — it is the map it draws when you scatter it on still water.' She opened the lid.
value:2.cnHint: 贝尔在搁浅的货船中发现了一罐发光粉末，她说它真正的____在于能在静水上显现地图，而非价钱。
value:2.hook: The map the dust drew pointed straight toward Silverfang's ship.
value:2.line: 'The *value* of a tool is what it opens, not what it costs,' Bell said.

sentences.en: Among the scattered cargo of a grounded sky-barge, Bell lifted a small jar of glowing amber dust.
sentences.cn: 在搁浅的天空货驳的散落货物中，小铃抱起一个装着发光琥珀色粉末的小罐子。

sentences.en: She held it to the starlight.
sentences.cn: 她把罐子举向星光。

sentences.en: 'The real *value* of this,' she said, 'is not what it sells for — it is the map it draws when you scatter it on still water.'
She opened the lid.
sentences.cn: 她打开了盖子。

connection:2.en: Old Helm pressed two broken halves of a carved stone tile together. They fit perfectly, and a thin line of light ran across the join. He said the *connection* between the two pieces completed an old route-sign, pointing toward the island Silverfang had claimed as his own by right of discovery.
connection:2.cnHint: 老舵将两块石板碎片拼合，碎片间的____让完整的路线标记重新发光，指向了银牙宣称发现的那座岛。
connection:2.hook: The route the stone pointed to was supposed to be a dead end.
connection:2.line: 'This *connection* between the pieces is the clue we needed,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: Old Helm pressed two broken halves of a carved stone tile together.
sentences.cn: 老舵把一块雕刻石板的两个断裂部分紧紧贴在一起。

sentences.en: They fit perfectly, and a thin line of light ran across the join.
sentences.cn: 它们完美地契合，一道细细的光线沿着接缝闪烁。

sentences.en: He said the *connection* between the two pieces completed an old route-sign, pointing toward the island Silverfang had claimed as his own by right of discovery.

story:2.en: On the underside of a floating rock shelf, someone had carved a short *story* in neat letters: a captain who won an island in a wager, then gave it back the next morning without a word. Old Helm read it twice. Bell and I looked at each other. We all knew who that captain was.
story:2.cnHint: 一块悬岩底面刻着一段短短的____，讲述一位船长赢得了一座岛却悄悄归还，我们都猜到了主角是谁。
story:2.hook: Below the carving, a single word was scratched deep: 'regret.'
story:2.line: 'Every *story* carved in stone was carved for a reason,' Old Helm said.

sentences.en: On the underside of a floating rock shelf, someone had carved a short *story* in neat letters: a captain who won an island in a wager, then gave it back the next morning without a word.
Old Helm read it twice.
sentences.cn: 老舵读了两遍。

sentences.en: Bell and I looked at each other.
sentences.cn: 小铃和我互相看了一眼。

sentences.en: We all knew who that captain was.
sentences.cn: 我们都知道那个船长是谁。

force:2.en: The locked chest sat at the centre of the Crystal Shelf island. Silverfang crossed his arms. 'I could *force* it open,' he said, eyeing the rusted lock. Old Helm shook his head and pointed to a keyhole shaped exactly like the word OPEN carved on its lid. Bell smiled, traced the letters, and the chest clicked free on its own.
force:2.cnHint: 银牙想用____打开箱子，但老舵发现了刻在锁孔上的线索。
force:2.hook: Inside the chest lay a map — but half of it was already gone.
force:2.line: 'I could *force* it open,' said Silverfang, 'but where is the fun in that?'

sentences.en: The locked chest sat at the centre of the Crystal Shelf island.
sentences.cn: 上锁的箱子摆在水晶架岛的中心。

sentences.en: Silverfang crossed his arms.
sentences.cn: 银牙交叉抱着手臂。

sentences.en: 'I could *force* it open,' he said, eyeing the rusted lock.
Old Helm shook his head and pointed to a keyhole shaped exactly like the word OPEN carved on its lid.
sentences.cn: 老舵摇了摇头，指向一个钥匙孔，形状正好像盖子上刻的"打开"这个词。

sentences.en: Bell smiled, traced the letters, and the chest clicked free on its own.
sentences.cn: 小铃笑了，用手指描过这些字母，箱子自己咔哒一声打开了。

importance:2.en: Bell found a brass plate half-buried in the soil of Windroot Isle. The words on it read: 'Know the *importance* of what you carry.' Old Helm knelt beside her, brushing away the moss. 'Every word fragment we collect,' he said softly, 'is someone's lost memory.' I held mine a little tighter after that.
importance:2.cnHint: 贝尔在风根岛发现了一块铜牌，提醒大家理解所携之物的____。
importance:2.hook: Below the brass plate, something else was buried — and it was still warm.
importance:2.line: 'Know the *importance* of what you carry,' Bell read aloud, her voice steady.

sentences.en: Bell found a brass plate half-buried in the soil of Windroot Isle.
sentences.cn: 小铃在风根岛的泥土里找到了一块黄铜牌子。

sentences.en: The words on it read: 'Know the *importance* of what you carry.'
Old Helm knelt beside her, brushing away the moss.
sentences.cn: 老舵跪在她身边，拨去苔藓。

sentences.en: 'Every word fragment we collect,' he said softly, 'is someone's lost memory.'
sentences.cn: "我们收集的每一个词语碎片，"他轻声说，"都是某个人丢失的记忆。"

sentences.en: I held mine a little tighter after that.
sentences.cn: 从那以后我握得更紧了。

sell:2.en: At the floating market above Amber Cove, a trader offered Old Helm a fat coin purse. 'I will buy that word fragment,' the trader said. Old Helm gave a slow *sell* — a tired smile that meant no deal was coming. 'These are not goods,' he said. 'They are doors.' The trader stared, then quietly stepped aside.
sell:2.cnHint: 在浮空市场，老舵用一个____的微笑拒绝了商人的收购提议。
sell:2.hook: The trader watched us leave, then pulled out a map of his own.
sell:2.line: Old Helm gave a slow *sell* of a smile and said, 'These are not for trade.'

sentences.en: At the floating market above Amber Cove, a trader offered Old Helm a fat coin purse.
sentences.cn: 在琥珀湾上方的漂浮市集，一个商人向老舵递出一个鼓囊囊的钱袋。

sentences.en: 'I will buy that word fragment,' the trader said.
sentences.cn: "我要买那个词语碎片，"商人说。

sentences.en: Old Helm gave a slow *sell* — a tired smile that meant no deal was coming.
'These are not goods,' he said.
sentences.cn: "这些不是商品，"他说。

sentences.en: 'They are doors.'
sentences.cn: "它们是门。"

sentences.en: The trader stared, then quietly stepped aside.
sentences.cn: 商人盯着看了一会儿，然后默默地退到了一边。

replace:2.en: One of our word fragments had cracked during the night crossing — the one that marked the path to Glasshorn Peak. Bell held up a smooth stone carved with the same letters. 'This will *replace* it for now,' she said. Old Helm nodded, though his eyes showed a flicker of worry. A copy was better than nothing. We hoped.
replace:2.cnHint: 贝尔用一块刻字石头____了夜渡中碎裂的词语碎片。
replace:2.hook: But when we pressed the copy to the map, the path it drew was slightly different.
replace:2.line: 'This will *replace* the broken one,' Bell said, pressing the stone into my hand.

sentences.en: One of our word fragments had cracked during the night crossing — the one that marked the path to Glasshorn Peak.
sentences.cn: 我们其中一个词语碎片在夜间穿越中裂了——那个标记通往玻璃角峰的路线的碎片。

sentences.en: Bell held up a smooth stone carved with the same letters.
sentences.cn: 小铃举起一块光滑的石头，上面刻着同样的字母。

sentences.en: 'This will *replace* it for now,' she said.
Old Helm nodded, though his eyes showed a flicker of worry.
sentences.cn: 老舵点了点头，不过眼睛里闪过一丝担忧。

sentences.en: A copy was better than nothing.
sentences.cn: 一份副本总比没有强。

sentences.en: We hoped.
sentences.cn: 我们希望如此。

approach:2.en: Old Helm gathered us at the bow as a new island drifted into view, its cliffs draped in soft silver light. 'Our *approach* matters here,' he said, unrolling the star chart. 'Come in from the east, low and slow, or the wind walls will push us back.' I watched Bell adjust the sails without a word. She already knew.
approach:2.cnHint: 老舵提醒大家靠近新岛屿时____很重要，需要从东侧低速切入。
approach:2.hook: From the east, I could see figures standing on the cliffs, already watching us.
approach:2.line: 'Our *approach* matters here,' Old Helm said, tapping the chart with one finger.

sentences.en: Old Helm gathered us at the bow as a new island drifted into view, its cliffs draped in soft silver light.
sentences.cn: 老舵在船首集合了我们，一座岛屿映入眼帘，悬崖被柔和的银光笼罩着。

sentences.en: 'Our *approach* matters here,' he said, unrolling the star chart.
'Come in from the east, low and slow, or the wind walls will push us back.'
sentences.cn: "从东边靠近，低空缓速，否则风墙会把我们推回去。"

sentences.en: I watched Bell adjust the sails without a word.
sentences.cn: 我看着小铃无言地调整船帆。

sentences.en: She already knew.
sentences.cn: 她已经知道了。

engage:2.en: Silverfang spotted a puzzle lock built into the gate of the Hollow Tower. Rather than wait for the others, he crouched and began to *engage* with it at once — turning each ring, listening for clicks, nose almost touching the metal. Old Helm and I exchanged a look. Whatever else Silverfang was, patient or reckless, he was never bored.
engage:2.cnHint: 银牙没有等其他人，独自____起了空心塔门上的密码锁。
engage:2.hook: The last ring turned — and the tower let out a sound like a held breath releasing.
engage:2.line: '*Engage* with the puzzle,' said Silverfang. 'Don't just stare at it.'

sentences.en: Silverfang spotted a puzzle lock built into the gate of the Hollow Tower.
sentences.cn: 银牙发现了空心塔大门上的一个谜题锁。

sentences.en: Rather than wait for the others, he crouched and began to *engage* with it at once — turning each ring, listening for clicks, nose almost touching the metal.
Old Helm and I exchanged a look.
sentences.cn: 老舵和我互相交换了一个眼神。

sentences.en: Whatever else Silverfang was, patient or reckless, he was never bored.
sentences.cn: 不管银牙还有什么其他特点，耐心还是鲁莽，他从不感到无聊。

ensure:2.en: Before we crossed the Fog Bridge to the next island, Bell walked its full length and back alone. 'I need to *ensure* it holds our weight,' she said. Old Helm waited without complaint. When she returned she gave one nod. We crossed in single file, the bridge swaying gently, and every step felt safe because she had already taken it.
ensure:2.cnHint: 贝尔独自走过雾桥，____桥身能承受众人的重量。
ensure:2.hook: Halfway across, I looked down — and saw a second bridge far below, broken and dark.
ensure:2.line: 'I need to *ensure* it holds,' Bell said, testing the first plank with her boot.

sentences.en: Before we crossed the Fog Bridge to the next island, Bell walked its full length and back alone.
sentences.cn: 在我们穿过迷雾桥前往下一个岛屿之前，小铃独自走过了整座桥，然后又走了回来。

sentences.en: 'I need to *ensure* it holds our weight,' she said.
Old Helm waited without complaint.
sentences.cn: 老舵没有怨言地等待。

sentences.en: When she returned she gave one nod.
sentences.cn: 她回来后给了一个点头。

sentences.en: We crossed in single file, the bridge swaying gently, and every step felt safe because she had already taken it.
sentences.cn: 我们单列纵队过了桥，桥在轻轻摇晃，每一步都感觉很安全，因为她已经踩过了。

limit:2.en: The word fragment for Ashpeak Island was locked behind a riddle: name the one thing that has no *limit*. Silverfang guessed gold. Old Helm guessed time. Bell said nothing for a long moment, then spoke one word quietly: 'curiosity.' The gate opened. Old Helm laughed, warm and low. I wrote the answer in my journal before I forgot it.
limit:2.cnHint: 谜题要求说出一件没有____的事物，贝尔的回答打开了大门。
limit:2.hook: Beyond the gate stood a library with no ceiling — just shelves rising into the stars.
limit:2.line: 'Name the one thing that has no *limit*,' the riddle asked, and Bell did not hesitate.

sentences.en: The word fragment for Ashpeak Island was locked behind a riddle: name the one thing that has no *limit*.
